newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SLIDES FURTHER ON KEY CURRENCIES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SLIDES FURTHER ON KEY CURRENCIES.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar continued falling against hard currencies on the back of import pressure on Monday, dealers said.
"The dollar continued its depreciatory trend today. I'm sure the Reserve Bank came into the market through one bank, but it didn't help much," one dealer said.
He added that most banks felt the central bank had not been doing enough over the past week to support the flagging currency.

"Everyone is quite cross about that. When they (central bank) eventually come into the market they are doing so in very small amounts. Today some guys were even threatening to go back to the two-point (bid/offer) spread (against the key U.S. dollar)," another dealer said.

The local unit finished the day at 11.1500/1600 against the U.S. dollar from last Friday's 11.1150/1250 and was also indicated weaker on sterling at 18.1500/1700 compared to 18.0100/0300 as it tracked a softer U.S. currency overseas.
Against the mark, it slipped to 6.6600/6800 from 6.6000/6200 and was at 2.5100/5300 from 2.4700/4900 versus the South African rand.
